title: agentic-foundation repository configuration (v2)
description: Schema for .agentic/config.yml — a platform-neutral contract for a graph of SDLC/STLC agent stages. Validated by the installer before rendering per-platform pipelines. Easy by default (a `profile` expands to a stage graph); granular when wanted (define `stages` explicitly). Any provider/model per stage; any SCM platform; any language. Secrets are referenced by NAME only; values never live here. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

extends.description: Base config(s) to inherit from, merged before this file (local values win). Layer an org base -> team base -> repo. A string or an ordered list of paths. Every base must resolve INSIDE the repository checkout (the project root) - vendor a shared org base into the repo (commit it, or fetch it at checkout) rather than pointing at an absolute or `../` path outside it; an out-of-repo base is rejected at load time. (`uri:` remote bases are not fetched offline.)

profile.description: Onboarding shortcut. Expands to a default stage graph you can then override via `stages`. `custom` adds no stages (you define them all).

platform.description: The SCM/CI platform this repo lives on. The contract is platform-neutral; a per-platform renderer maps it to that system's pipeline. (GitHub renderer ships first.)

host.description: For self-hosted / enterprise (e.g. github.example.com, a self-managed GitLab, dev.azure.com/org). Blank = the platform's public host.

trusted_roles.description: Normalized author-permission levels allowed to drive agentic changes; the renderer maps them to the platform's own roles.

token_secret.description: NAME of the secret holding the platform API token. Never the value.

defaults.description: Org/account-level fallbacks. A stage that does not set its own provider/model resolves here; if nothing resolves the run fails loudly (there is no hidden toolkit fallback).

provider.description: Default provider id for stages that omit one. Supported today: `anthropic` (runs Claude Code) and `openai` (runs Codex). Other ids are accepted for forward-compatibility but not rendered yet.

models.description: Default model binding per provider id (open map — any provider).
Provider-agnostic model aliases. Reference an alias name anywhere a model is expected and map it per provider here, so model-ID churn touches one place.

providers.description: Per-provider connection settings, keyed by provider id (open map — anthropic, openai, gemini, azure_openai, bedrock, vertex, ollama, openai_compatible, custom, ...). Endpoint/version/deployment plus the NAME of the key secret. Lets you point at self-hosted / cloud / proxy / on-prem gateways. Never a secret value.

skills.description: Skill registry, keyed by skill id. A skill is the reusable methodology/content for a stage (checklist, rubric, output format) — provider-, backend-, and language-agnostic. Register your own or override a shipped one by id. Built-ins live in templates/skills/<id>/. Referenced from stages via `stages[].skill`.

stages.description: The agent pipeline as an ordered, extensible graph. Each stage is one agent bound to a provider+model (the tool is derived from the provider). Merged onto the `profile`'s stages (a stage here with the same id overrides the profile's).

tiering.description: Global deterministic model tiering (change size + paths -> trivial/standard/complex), reused with no extra model call. A stage may opt out with `tiering: false`.

guardrails.description: Prompt-injection / untrusted-input controls. Content from PRs/MRs, issues, comments, and diffs is treated as data, not instructions.

observability.description: Where run records go. Adapts to your stack — file, CI artifact, webhook, or OTLP collector — with endpoints supplied by variable/secret NAME, never hardcoded. Secrets are always redacted from output.

build.description: What "green" means for THIS repository. Optional: omit it for a repo with no build gate (e.g. docs-only). Language-agnostic — stages run exactly what is set here and assume no language.

enabled.description: Set false to disable the fast-path lane so every PR (docs included) is routed to the reviewer.

merge.description: Merge-gate policy for the auto-merge lane (only meaningful when modules.auto_merge is true).

name.description: Exact check-run name the external tool publishes (e.g. "SonarCloud Code Analysis").

app_id.description: Immutable numeric GitHub App REGISTRATION id that must be the check-run's producer (matched against the check-run's .app.id — NOT the App's bot-user id). Required because App slugs are mutable and a display name alone is not an identity. Read it from a check-run the tool posted (e.g. repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/SHA/check-runs -> .check_runs[].app.id) or the App's registration page. A same-name check from any other App (including github-actions) does not satisfy the requirement.

required_status_checks.description: External status check-runs (e.g. a SonarCloud / SonarQube / Checkmarx check) that must be present and green on the PR head before auto-merge, identified by exact name AND producing App id. stagr does not run these tools; it only requires their result. Default: none.

protected_paths.description: Paths whose modification forces human review: if a PR changes any matching file, the auto-merge gate refuses to auto-merge and leaves the PR for a human (same effect as the human-merge label). These are the security-sensitive control plane — CI/gate workflow definitions and the toolkit config/contract — whose changes need human judgment and which the gate cannot authenticate by content. Each entry is EITHER an exact file path (e.g. '.github/workflows/validate.yml') OR a directory prefix ending in '/**' (e.g. '.github/workflows/**', which matches any file at or below that directory), matched deterministically by equality/prefix. General globs ('**/*.yml', '*', '?', mid-pattern '**', braces) are NOT supported (the gate's shell cannot match them reliably) and are rejected at validation. Default: ['.github/workflows/**', '.agentic/**']. Set to [] only if you accept auto-merging changes to your own gate.

method.description: The merge method the auto-merge gate uses. The target repository must have this method enabled or GitHub rejects every merge. Default: squash.

stage.description: One agent in the pipeline. `id` is always required; `type` is required unless `from` supplies it via an agent preset. Provider/model resolve through the precedence chain; the executor/tool is derived from the provider unless `backend` pins one.

id.description: Unique stage id, e.g. plan, implement, security, integration-test.

type.description: Semantic role; drives sensible defaults (e.g. review/security/test default to a blocking gate; plan/docs to advisory).

from.description: Agent-preset id to base this stage on (from templates/agents/). Fields set here override the preset.

provider.description: Provider id for this stage; the primary knob. Supported today: `anthropic` (runs Claude Code — implement stages) and `openai` (runs Codex — review/security stages). The executor/tool is derived from this, so a stage normally sets only `provider` + `model` and omits `backend`. Omit `provider` to inherit defaults.provider.

skill.description: Skill id (from `skills` registry or a built-in) supplying this stage's methodology. Takes precedence over inline `instructions`.

gate.description: advisory = comment only; blocking = emits a required status check. Omit to use the type's default.

depends_on.description: Ids of stages that must run before this one (defines the graph).

instructions.description: Inline prompt/policy for the stage, or a path to a prompt file.

backend.description: Optional executor override. Normally omit it — the tool is derived from `provider` (`anthropic` -> Claude Code, `openai` -> Codex). Set it only to pin a specific tool or point at a custom adapter. Rendered today: `claude-code-action` (the Anthropic implementer) and `codex` (the OpenAI review/security lane). The remaining names are accepted so configs stay forward-compatible but are roadmap: `generic` (a provider-agnostic runner via a user-supplied adapter), `openhands`, `pr-agent`, `swe-agent`, `custom`, and `claude-code-cli` (a CLI-in-runner adapter for Claude Code, Phase 3). `with` carries backend-specific inputs; `uses` overrides the action/image for `custom`.

uses.description: Action ref or container image (for `custom`, or to pin/override an adapter).

with.description: Backend-specific inputs passed through to the executor.

budgets.description: Cost / token ceilings. All limits are opt-in; set only what you want enforced. Usable globally or per-stage.

max_review_iterations.description: Maximum number of review→fix cycles per PR before the lane stops and escalates. Opt-in; the field only declares the cap — enforcement is rendered separately (see docs/stagr/governance-and-limits.md).

modelBinding.description: Optional model binding. Every field is optional so a caller can override only what they need (e.g. just the `complex` tier). A value may be a literal model ID or an alias name from `models.aliases`.

skillRef.description: A registry entry pointing at a skill's content. `builtin` uses templates/skills/<id>/; `path`/`uri` load your own; `extends` layers this skill on top of another (base first, this overrides).

extends.description: Base skill id this one extends.

modelAlias.description: One alias mapped to a concrete model ID per provider id (open map).

providerConn.description: Provider connection settings. Contains NO secret values — only the name of the secret to read.

observabilitySink.description: A single destination for run records. `endpoint_var`/`headers_secret` are NAMES of a variable/secret, so the actual URL and token stay out of config.
